summary: A shell of gas blown by the fast wind of the Wolf-Rayet star WR 136 into the material it shed as a red giant, glowing in hydrogen-alpha with a thin skin of doubly ionised oxygen.

sections.title: What it is
paragraphs: Example text for the test fixture: the shell formed when the star's Wolf-Rayet wind caught up with slower material.

sections.title: Discovery
paragraphs: Example text: catalogued by William Herschel in 1792.

imaging_notes: The OIII skin is faint: D1 nights carry most of the signal.
Dense star field: StarXTerminator before stretching.
